findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: In updateEvent, selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is falsy the else-branch searches for cal.externalId === externalCalendarId (null/undefined/empty), so it always yields undefined. Updates for bookings without an externalCalendarId therefore call calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined instead of falling back to the destination calendar, causing update failures.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: In deleteEvent, calendarId uses the same pattern: externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is missing the find predicate compares against the same missing value and returns undefined, so deletion falls back to primary even when a destinationCalendar is present, deleting from / missing the event on the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Unhandled undefined when no destinationCalendar breaks Google Meet fallback
findings.body: const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [] followed by mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar" dereferences possibly-undefined. When evt has no destination calendar (empty array, which this PR now explicitly creates), this throws TypeError and breaks all event creation, instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Collective destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither eventType nor organizer has a calendar, then evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is used for COLLECTIVE events. Optional chaining on null is a no-op, so hosts' destination calendars collected in teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and only the organizer calendar (none) is used. Collective hosts then never get calendar events created. It should initialize to [] not null.

findings.title: Webhook payload contract changed without updating all expectations
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from object/null to array, so webhook payloads now emit [] instead of null. This test still asserts destinationCalendar: null for BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED (lines 119, 373) while only BOOKING_REJECTED was updated to []. This is a breaking change for webhook consumers and leaves stale assertions that will fail / mask the new shape.
